question: is there a public individual-level panel of the person's declared group for the polygenic scores lane-pgs left UNKNOWN?
declared_group_source: the ancestry the GIAB donors declared (lane-pgs's DECLARED); never inferred, and never replaced by a group a panel does cover

gate.min_people_reads: at least 100 people carrying the declared group's label in the panel, unrelated to each other and to the person. At 100 people an empirical percentile near the middle carries a 95% binomial interval of about +/-10 points (1.96 * sqrt(0.25 / 100) = 0.098), and the chi-square interval of a variance read from them spans about [0.77, 1.35] times the estimate (df 99), against [0.70, 1.77] for the 39 HPRC people lane-pgs had (df 37), whose lower bound for height-3290 sat at 1.016
gate.access_reads: the per-person genotypes download without an application, a data-access committee, a signed letter, a login, or a request to the authors, under terms that permit research use; anything else fails the gate whatever its size
gate.individual_level: per-person genotypes (sequence or array calls) are released; aggregate allele frequencies, which lane-pgs already uses, do not qualify
gate.label: a panel person belongs to the declared group only through the panel's OWN population label (the sampling population the panel publishes): for asj, a label naming Ashkenazi Jews (ASJ_LABEL); for the other gnomAD groups, the frozen 1000 Genomes code table THOUSAND_GROUP. No person, panel or HG002, is assigned to a group by genetic similarity, and HG002's declared group (asj, as its donors declared) is never replaced by one a panel covers
gate.unrelated: people are counted once per family: a panel's own unrelated set where it publishes one (1000 Genomes phase 3's 2,504), founders only in a trio, and the person and the person's first-degree relatives (RELATIVES) never
gate.coverage: evaluated only for a candidate that meets access, individual level, label and size: the score's variants with a directly called genotype in the panel's release (no imputation) must carry at least coverage_floor of the score's total |weight|, the bar lane-pgs used
gate.stop: if no candidate meets the gate for the person's declared group, the lane stops and the inventory is the result: nothing is registered, no score is computed on any panel, and the person's UNKNOWN for PGS000297 and PGS000018 stands
gate.other_groups: for every other gnomAD group the inventory records which candidates meet access, individual level, label and size (coverage not evaluated): what a later registration could use for a person who declares that group. Descriptive; no score is computed

scores_left_unknown.PGS000018: metaGRS (coronary artery disease), 1,745,158 variants: R1 3.19 [2.12, 5.34], independence fails, and above the 20,000-variant per-variant lookup cap

note: a percentile is a position among people of the stated group on one score; it is not a risk. The other_groups counts are descriptive: no score is computed for anyone
reading: No public individual-level panel qualifies for Ashkenazi Jewish (asj): of 12 candidates examined, the largest count of people carrying that group's own label in an openly downloadable release is 21 (ebc_jew2010), against the gate's minimum of 100 fixed before these counts were taken. The one panel of that group at the required size is controlled-access (tagc, 128 samples, EGA EGAD00001000781 under data-access committee EGAC00001000151), which the lane may not apply for. Nothing is registered, no score is computed on any panel, and the person's UNKNOWN for PGS000297 (height, 3,290 SNPs), PGS000018 (metaGRS (coronary artery disease), 1,745,158 variants) stands. This is a statement about what is published, not about the person.

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record 854e200

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
